I found no claim to flag in the document. Every factual claim matches a line of the record, and neither went_wrong item is one its field excludes.

- **Spread of the flag change:** The flag went from off to on for every evaluation within about a minute. During 15:47, 16 of 200 evaluations read on (G971b); from 15:48 all 200 did (Gce95). So "starting in that minute" and "at once" hold.
- **The code reading:** The root cause and the arithmetic in the causal chain rest on Code-Fix's reading (F1). The document cites F1 and says nothing ran it, so the root cause is marked unverified, and "likely" hedges the plain-words version.
- **Left unjudged:**
  - The "stops the harm" and "why it did not help" fields only give directions for what to do, so I didn't judge them.
  - I also didn't judge the "had it been otherwise" sentences, which are what-ifs. That includes the clause about a person joining only when the draft pull request was left for review.
  - The action items aren't judged either.

supported.quote: With monthly-spend-feature on, `render_spend_summary` sends the account page request to `average_spend_per_item_this_month`, which divides the month's total spend by the number of purchases flagged `in_current_month`. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month that number is zero, so the request raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and the account page fails. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.

Account pages started failing when a setting switched on a new monthly spending summary, and that summary likely breaks for shoppers who have bought before but nothing this month, because it divides by the number of this month's purchases.
Account page requests could go on failing with the division-by-zero error at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 while monthly-spend-feature stays on, and it was left on.
Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the share of failed account page requests in the minute rose far above its usual level.
The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError (division by zero) at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. These errors started in the minute of the onset and were not seen before it.

An admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. Flag evaluations went from all off to all on starting in that minute, so account page requests began running the spend summary code path that the flag turns on.
The service with the flag off: before the onset every evaluation read off, account pages rendered normally, and the error rate was typically low.
Shoppers closing the connection: these ClientDisconnected failures were already being logged during the healthy stretch before the onset, while the error rate stayed typically low.
The spend summary path divides by the number of purchases made this month, and that number is zero for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.
monthly-spend-feature went from off to on for every evaluation at once. No staged rollout to a small share of traffic was seen.
Before the flag was switched on in production, no check was seen that ran the code path it turns on for a shopper with past purchases but none this month.
Nobody was paged: HighErrorRate on io-shop was not linked to any on-call incident.
